meta_title: Pepperi Alternative for Food Distributors in 2026
meta_desc: Your accounts speak each order into the app and approve the lines before it sends. A Pepperi alternative for small to mid-size food distributors.

hero.h1: A Pepperi Alternative Built For The Reorder.
hero.lead: VOS is for the reorder nobody had to go and collect. A customer talks the order into the app, checks the lines, and sends it. Pepperi arms the people who go out to your accounts: routes, shelf audits, promotions. Nobody has to stop by to write this one up.

problem.h2: Why distributors look at an alternative to Pepperi
problem.lead: Hardly anybody searching for a Pepperi competitor wants to rebuild how their sales force works. They want one part of the week to stop costing so much. Three such cases turn up a lot, and they are worth keeping apart.

cards.h3: The product is wider than the problem
cards.body: Pepperi carries route accounting, retail execution, promotions, CRM and analytics. If what you came for was a better way to receive orders, you are being asked to weigh up a platform decision to get at one of its channels.

cards.h3: A storefront does not end the calls
cards.body: Self-service ordering only helps with the accounts who use it. The rest ring the desk at the worst hour of the day, and somebody keys those in by hand regardless of what the portal cost.

cards.h3: Nobody is visiting a kitchen every week
cards.body: Shelf audits and merchandising matter when your product sits in a store. A chef reordering the same forty lines every week is a different motion, and much of that toolkit may never be opened.

features.h2: What a Pepperi alternative actually changes

rows.h3: A chef talks, and that is the order
rows.body: No search field, no quantity box, no screen anybody has to be trained on. They walk the cooler, say what is short, and the items come up as a list. They correct whatever looks wrong and send it. That is the step a portal does not always win over.
bullets: The buyer reads the lines before anything leaves
Said from a walk-in or an office, at any hour
Their own handset, iOS or Android, nothing issued
20 to 30 minutes back against the same order by phone
Reorders from accounts on the app stop reaching your reps, so that time goes into selling

rows.h3: One list per account, priced the way you priced it
rows.body: Send over the lists you keep today. Each account gets the items it buys against your codes, at the figure you hold for that customer, and setup is done. You keep the catalog and the pricing; they get the convenience.
bullets: A kitchen never sees a line it does not buy
Nobody else is promoting into your customer's list
Edit a guide once and the next order already has it
Your team works in the same admin platform, account by account

rows.h3: It turns up the way your office already works
rows.body: A finished order goes out as an email carrying a PDF, Excel or Word file, or straight into your system over the API, over EDI, or into QuickBooks. Whichever route your desk already trusts is the route it takes.
bullets: Sent to a named rep, or to the purchasing desk
On a direct feed nobody retypes it at your end
Its own number, with the date and time it was sent
Picking, billing and delivery go on exactly as now

rows.h3: Stock in view as the orders come in
rows.body: VOS carries real-time inventory visibility tied to order activity, and the catalog updates as stock levels change. It is not the system of record for stock: the one you run today stays in charge, and a demo shows how the levels connect.
bullets: The whole catalog, not just the fast movers
Fewer stockout surprises on a late, heavy order
Levels come from the system you count with now
No counting and no buying happens inside VOS

cards.h2: When VOS and Pepperi work together
cards.lead: That is the common case here, not the exception. VOS is no sort of Pepperi replacement: your field team keeps its routes, its audits and its promotions, and the orders that never needed a visit arrive on their own. For most distributors that is what a Pepperi alternative turns out to mean.

items.h3: Your reps keep every tool they have
items.body: Routes, audits, van stock and promotions carry on where they are. VOS takes nothing out of a rep's hands. It just stops the app accounts' reorders landing there first.

items.h3: Self-service keeps the accounts that like it
items.body: Buyers who are happy clicking through a catalog should carry on. This is for the part of the book that never took to one and still telephones instead.

items.h3: Start with the accounts nobody gets around to visiting
items.body: Pick the kitchens your reps rarely reach and open those first. Nothing about the territory or the route plan has to change to try it.

midcta.h3: See one order go the whole way through
midcta.body: Twenty minutes. A chef speaks one, you see how it reaches the desk laid out as your desk reads it, and how much of that stops landing on your desk.

steps.h2: Three steps, and no rollout to manage
steps.lead: There is no territory to map and no team to train. You hand over the lists, we open the accounts, your customers start ordering.

items.body: A spreadsheet is plenty. Items and the price per account load into one admin screen, against the codes you already use.
Logins get created and the kitchen is shown the app once. Most of them send something in before the day is out.
Approved by the buyer, carrying a number and a time, laid out as your office expects.

comparison.h2: VoiceOrder Solutions vs Pepperi. Built for different moments.
comparison.lead: In VOS the repeat order happens without a rep attending it. Pepperi is a field sales platform covering van routes, store audits, promotions and CRM, so a Pepperi alternative is a question about which moment you are buying for. The table sets the two jobs against each other.

faq.h2: What distributors with field reps ask us

items.q: Is VOS a Pepperi alternative, or another sort of product?
items.a: Quite a different thing, and it is better to be blunt about that. Pepperi serves your sales organization: the rep, the van and the shelf. VOS deals only with how the order gets to you. Treat them as equivalents and one of them will let you down, so the better question is which part of the week hurts.

At pulling an order out of a kitchen that will never log in, we think so. At everything else on their product list the question does not really apply: we have no route accounting, no store audits, no CRM and no promotion engine, and none of it is planned.

items.q: Does Pepperi not already let customers order for themselves?
items.a: It does, and anyone who tells you otherwise has not read their site. They offer a branded self-service portal with each buyer's own catalog and pricing. Every route into it still means working a screen: searching the catalog, scanning a barcode or uploading a file. The accounts that were not going to do that are the ones this suits.

items.q: Do we give up route accounting and van sales?
items.a: Only if you drop the tool that does them, and we are not asking you to. VOS has never planned a route, loaded a van or reconciled a day's selling, and it does not track a shipment either. If those are what you are shopping for, Pepperi is the right call and we will say so.

items.q: We are a smaller operation. Does that change the answer?
items.a: It is most of the answer. Their own site describes their customers as medium and enterprise. Ours says we are built for small to mid-size distributors, and that enterprise pricing and enterprise complexity are not your problem. Both companies are telling you who they are for, and it is worth taking them at their word.

Pepperi publishes no price on its own site, and nor do we. Be aware that third-party directories carry figures for them, so check any number you are shown against their own site. What we will say is that the scope is narrower here: you are buying one step, not the system your field force lives in.

items.q: How fast could this be running?
items.a: For most distributors this is running in 24 to 48 hours, and most kitchens get a first order in the same day. There is no integration project, which is why a Pepperi alternative often gets shortlisted by people with no intention of replacing anything.

items.q: What about accounts that will only ever telephone?
items.a: They go on telephoning, and your desk handles those as always. Be clear on the limit, though: a call or a voicemail gets no order number out of VOS, no timestamp, and nothing moving against stock. Only what comes through the app does.

items.q: Where do the Pepperi details on this page come from?
items.a: Sourced from pepperi.com as it stood on 10 October 2026: their product modules, the buyer portal, the offline apps and their own words about the market they sell to. No price or rollout time is published by them, so neither is guessed at here. Anything out of date since is our error, not theirs.

mainCta.body: Twenty minutes, one reorder that nobody had to drive out for.
